report = scheduled departure - 60 min (assumption); PLT-CREW-DUTY: in-block (landing slot + ROT + taxi-in, or the alternate arrival for a diversion) must be within the duty end. A flight whose earliest possible in-block (minimum over the open runways of the runway-dependent earliest landing + ROT + unimpeded routed taxi to the plan's gate, the scheduled gate for a diversion; replaces v2's ETA + taxi, and far taxi for diversions) is already past the duty end is an unavoidable duty bust (data): reported in the check detail, never a violation. Otherwise the rule fails iff the plan's arrival is past the duty end. Skipped when the departure time is unknown

limits.value: fastest route on the OpenStreetMap taxiway graph, runway exit to the gate's stand; in-block = landing slot + ROT + taxi
limits.note: taxiways, stands, runway exits and holding positions from OSM (ODbL); gates bound to OSM stands (ref, then nearest within 150 m, else a generic stand); 20 kt, 10 kt on taxilanes and turns > 30 deg, +30 s to park (assumptions); exit = first forward exit past the required roll (narrow 1,500 m, wide 2,000 m, x1.15 wet), exits whose taxi network holds no stand skipped; ROT = 2d / (v_td + v_exit), v_exit 25 kt (exit <= 45 deg) or 12 kt; ATC-TAXI-ROUTE fails when no exit of the runway end reaches the stand. Quality gate per wave: every open runway end in OSM reaches >= 80 % of the wave's bound stands, else the wave uses the generic estimate (straight line runway midpoint -> gate x1.4 at 15 kt, generic exit at the required roll and 12 kt; assumption). Runways without coordinates keep v2's 6 min near / 10 min far. Remote stand: + 10 min bus. No taxiway closures modelled. taxi = unimpeded + the hold-short / give-way waits of the plan's hold-short pass (ATC-TAXI-CONFLICT); no ramp or gate waits, so it can sit below BTS TAXI_IN (FCFS medians on the replays with the 2015 movements, ROT + taxi + waits vs taxi-in reference: ORD 4.1 / 26.0, MIA 5.0 / 4.0, ATL 4.6 / 16.0, DFW 16.4 / 13.5, DEN 6.4 / 5.5 min; DFW is above the reference because three arrivals wait head-on against a 36R departure stream on their fixed route, no rerouting: see 'departure holding bay'); see the taxi validation (Task 27)

ATC-TAXI-CONFLICT (FAA JO 7110.65 §3-7-2: ground control issues the route and hold-short instructions): wave flights move along their fixed route (no rerouting) in runway-exit order and wait at the previous node, or at the hold before a runway's zone, until every node is clear of the fixed traffic and earlier wave flights by this headway and no edge is in use head-on. Fixed traffic (queue arrivals, real 2015 departures) is scheduled once per wave and never yields

limits.value: no landing on the crossed strip from 1.5 min before to 1 min after the time in its zone; no takeoff within 1 min either side
limits.note: the whole time inside the strip's protected zone (from leaving the hold to past the zone) is checked against the fixed traffic's landings and takeoffs and every landing of the plan, for the wave flights

limits.value: landing priority; fixed 2015 crossers are not re-timed per plan
limits.note: the fixed traffic (queue arrivals, real 2015 departures) is scheduled once per wave, before any plan exists. When a plan landing falls in the crossing gap window of a scheduled fixed crossing of that strip, a controller would hold the crosser, never the arrival: it does not fail ATC-TAXI-CONFLICT and is reported as an informational conflict (kind fixed_holds_for_landing: fixed callsign, strip, the hold it would need, until 1 min after the landing; evidence fixed_holds). The fixed track and its knock-on effects are not re-timed. A plan landing while a fixed arrival is still on that runway does fail (same-runway separation, evidence landing_conflicts)

limits.value: landing priority; a fixed takeoff less than 1 min before a plan landing on its strip would be held
limits.note: the fixed takeoffs are timed once when the wave is built (takeoff spacing, the queue arrivals' landings, scheduled crossings), never from any wave flight's landing, FCFS or plan. A plan landing less than the landing / takeoff gap after a fixed takeoff on the same strip does not fail ATC-TAXI-CONFLICT: a controller would hold the departure. It is an informational conflict (kind fixed_departure_holds: fixed callsign, strip, the hold until the gap after the landing; evidence fixed_departure_holds); the fixed departure is not re-timed for it. A fixed takeoff at or after the landing while the wave flight is still on the runway fails the runway-vacate rule
a wave flight whose total taxi wait exceeds it (or whose route starts inside another strip's zone during a landing or takeoff) fails ATC-TAXI-CONFLICT; shorter waits never fail, they add to in-block

limits.value: clear of the runway before the next landing or takeoff on that strip
limits.note: FAA JO 7110.65 §3-10-3 (same-runway separation: the preceding aircraft has taxied off before the next crosses the threshold). ATC-TAXI-CONFLICT fails when a wave flight's exit clear time (first node past the exit runway's 90 m zone and off every runway's pavement) is after another flight's landing or takeoff on that strip, counted from its own landing. No pre-landing margin (unlike the crossing gap): the same-runway rule sets none, and the independent verifier's runway-vacate check uses the same window, so every verifier 'still vacating' message on a wave flight is a failing check

limits.limit: landing / takeoff gap on one runway
limits.note: mixed mode (fixed departures sharing the arrival runway): a fixed takeoff stays 1 min from every landing on its strip (the arrival has vacated, or the departure is airborne before the arrival crosses the threshold). A wave landing against fixed takeoffs on the same strip: a takeoff while the wave flight is still on the runway fails the runway-vacate rule; a takeoff less than 1 min before the landing is landing priority (informational fixed_departure_holds, see 'fixed departures vs plan landings')

limits.value: 3 aircraft per holding point, resequenced by takeoff time; beyond that the queue backs up upstream
limits.note: real ATC resequences departures at the runway (holding bays let an aircraft with an earlier slot pass one that is waiting; controller ruling T31). A fixed departure that reaches its holding point before its takeoff waits in the bay until it lines up 30 s before takeoff: off the taxiway (no node reservation), so it blocks neither a later departure with an earlier takeoff nor the wave flights. At most 3 wait at once per holding point (bay capacity, assumption); the next one waits upstream on the taxiway until one leaves (re-scheduled behind it, visible to every later mover and to the wave flights). Takeoffs are spaced only from takeoffs already settled in pushback order. Replays with the 2015 movements (bay wait median / p95 / max; upstream queue wait median / max; fixed movers over the 30-min horizon): ORD 4.0 / 94.6 / 125.2, 27.8 / 91.7, 41; MIA 10.7 / 17.9 / 38.3, 0 / 8.6, 0; ATL 5.0 / 17.0 / 22.0, 7.6 / 23.3, 0; DFW 5.0 / 18.0 / 39.0, 2.3 / 12.6, 0; DEN 9.3 / 22.4 / 23.2, 0 / 7.0, 0. Known limitation: the ORD replay overloads the fixed traffic: it sends 88 departures to 27R/28C/28R and 41 of them wait past the horizon (the count is in the wave's ground-traffic provenance). Pushback is WHEELS_OFF - TAXI_OUT, and BTS TAXI_OUT already contains the real queue, so the bay wait stands for that queue. Wave arrivals giving way to a departure on a shared taxiway (FCFS plans): DFW 3, other replays 0. Known limitation: the DFW waits (MQ2833 21.0, AA2441 13.6, AA260 7.6 min, all at node 107) are head-on waits on the arrival's fixed route against a stream of 36R departures (9-10 departures on its route edges, opposite direction, during each wait); with no rerouting the arrival waits for a gap, and its ROT + taxi + wait exceeds its own BTS TAXI_IN (19.3 / 15.0, 13.5 / 9.0, 26.7 / 16.0 min)

limits.value: 90 m from a crossed runway's centreline
limits.note: taxiing aircraft never wait closer than this to a runway they cross, except at an OSM holding position off the pavement; on the pavement = within 45 m of the centreline

limits.value: AIM 5-3-8: 200 KIAS <= 6,000 ft, 230 KIAS to 14,000 ft, 265 KIAS above; inbound leg 1.0 min <= 14,000 ft, 1.5 min above; right turns unless published
limits.note: published (CIFP HF/HM/HA) hold geometry where coded, else a standard hold at the STAR fix; turn rate = least bank of 3 deg/s, 30 deg, 25 deg; TAS = IAS x (1 + 0.02 x alt/1000); lap time derived from these; hold_min = laps x lap_min + vector stretch

1,000 ft vertical spacing per FAA JO 7110.65 §4-5-1, first come first served per §2-1-4; the 5-level depth is our assumption; only flights with >= 1 whole lap enter the stack; ATC-HOLD-STACK fails a 6th simultaneous holder and a later entrant leaving while an earlier one still holds

limits.value: workbook holding burn for route extra and holding
limits.note: fuel_kg = (hold_min + route_extra_min) x holding burn (route extra may be negative, never below zero fuel); PLT-FUEL-RESERVE checks hold_min + max(0, route_extra_min) <= extra fuel

limits.value: 280 KIAS above 10,000 ft, 250 below, 210 from the IAF, 170 at the FAF, 140 kt final
limits.note: converted to TAS for route time T_route; METAR headwind applied on final only; the runway-dependent earliest landing is t_entry + SR + GD + T_route(runway) with t_entry = ETA - T_route(FCFS runway)
current procedures (CIFP 2611) flown over 2015 traffic; not for navigation

limits.value: the flow's free parallel ends plus free non-crossing ends within 60 deg (segregated), else the arrival runway (mixed mode); earliest expected takeoff
limits.note: fixed ground traffic (real BTS 2015 departures, wheels-off T-30..T+120): the departure candidates are every open runway end free of arrivals that is parallel to the majority FCFS arrival runway (heading within 10 deg, same direction, another strip), plus every other free open end within 60 deg of it with no tailwind whose centreline crosses no arrival strip and no strip already chosen (nearest heading first; crossing-runway operations are not modelled). Mixed mode (departures share the arrival runway) iff there is none. Replays: ORD arrivals 32R, departures 27R/28C/28R; DFW arrivals 35C, departures 31L/31R/36L/36R; MIA arrivals 08L, departures 09; ATL arrivals 08L, departures 09L/09R; DEN arrivals 16L, departures 17L/17R. In pushback order each departure is trial-scheduled (hold-short scheduler, crossing waits and queues included) to every candidate and takes the earliest expected takeoff: leaving the holding point, never before WHEELS_OFF, spaced from the strip's other takeoffs (departure takeoff spacing); a schedule that is not ok, or a takeoff inside an already scheduled crossing's window, ranks last; ties to the threshold nearest its (seeded, simulated) stand, then runway id. Pushback = WHEELS_OFF - TAXI_OUT; the departure waits in the holding bay until it lines up 30 s before takeoff (departure holding bay); takeoff at WHEELS_OFF, later only if taxi waits, takeoff spacing, a landing on its strip or a scheduled crossing hold it. Known limitation: arrival runways are v2's FCFS choice (queue on the two best-wind ends), so e.g. ATL east flow lands on 08L/08R in this model, whereas real ATL lands on the outboard runways (08L, 09R, 10) and departs from 08R/09L

limits.value: 1 takeoff per minute per runway end
limits.note: a departure's recorded takeoff is the earliest time >= max(WHEELS_OFF, leaving the holding point) that is 1 min from every other takeoff on the strip and outside every scheduled crossing's gap window (the departure waits at the holding point: FCFS, the crosser came first); the runway choice uses the same time; it is spaced only from takeoffs already settled in pushback order and from every landing on the strip (1 min). It matches the holding-point throughput of the ground scheduler (30 s node headway + 30 s line-up). Replays with the 2015 movements, takeoffs later than WHEELS_OFF (> 0 / > 1 / > 5 min, max): ORD 39 / 38 / 31 of 88, 36.0; MIA 2 / 0 / 0 of 24, 1.0; ATL 38 / 33 / 18 of 110, 16.0; DFW 4 / 4 / 0 of 119, 4.0; DEN 0 of 24
